data.reason: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 has a stuck transmit queue (repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flaps), so the host can no longer send anything out the WAN side even though the interface is UP with a valid address and route; the upstream provider path itself recovered hours ago.

data.cause: The firewall's WAN interface vtnet0 has a stuck transmit queue (repeated "watchdog timeout on queue 0" with link DOWN/UP flaps), so the host can no longer send anything out the WAN side even though the interface is UP with a valid address and route; the upstream provider path itself recovered hours ago.
evidence: dmesg -a: repeated 'vtnet0: watchdog timeout on queue 0' interleaved with 'vtnet0: link state changed to DOWN/UP' - the WAN NIC driver stopped draining its TX queue and the link kept re-negotiating.
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1 and ping -c 3 -n 1.1.1.1: 'ping: sendto: No buffer space available', 100% loss - sends fail locally at the stalled interface rather than being answered downstream.
arp -a -n: '? (198.51.100.1) at (incomplete) on vtnet0 expired' - no ARP resolution of the ISP gateway, consistent with a dead TX path; the LAN entry (10.20.0.9) is fine.
ifconfig vtnet0 / netstat -rn: interface UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP with lease 198.51.100.27 and default via 198.51.100.1 still present, so addressing/routing are intact - the failure is below IP.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/state.json + events.jsonl: outage_start ~02:01-02:06, reloads_in_outage=4 all rc=0, then at 03:30 decision action=none reason=reload_cap (reloads_24h=12/12). WAN renews were performed repeatedly and did not restore traffic, so the lease is not the fault.

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl + modem-metrics.jsonl: 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out' at 02:01:44 triggered the drop, but 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete' at 02:28:21 and cm_status=OPERATIONAL at 02:30, 03:00 and 03:30 show the modem/provider side recovered while the internet stayed down on gw.lan.
data.recommendation: Reboot the firewall gw.lan to reset the hung vtnet0 interface/driver; its WAN DHCP lease and routing are fine and a plain wan_reload has already been run 4 times this outage (12/12 of the 24h cap) with no recovery, so only a full host reset will clear the stuck queue. The maintainer is away, so let the harness decide per its conditions. Afterwards, if the same watchdog timeouts recur on this NIC, investigate the virtio WAN device/driver rather than reloading the interface.
data.detail: vtnet0 WAN NIC/driver transmit queue hung (watchdog timeouts), link flapping
